clips.caption:
Charlie Munger said the best investors aren't the smartest - they're the calmest.

A former Navy SEAL explains why: equanimity. The ability to stay level whether things are going great or falling apart.

In SEAL training they test for it every single day. Crack under pressure once and you go home.

Years later his girlfriend called crying over a flat tire on the highway. He told her the truth: no amount of tears was going to fix that tire.

Not because he didn't care. Because panic never solved anything - action did.

Where in your life are you crying over the flat tire instead of fixing it?

clips.caption:
A 10-time world pool champion forgot one of his biggest losses completely.

Mike Siegel couldn't even remember blowing a game to Efren Reyes. But ask him about the time he came back from down nine games to none against Johnny Archer and won - he remembers every shot.

Same facts, different story. A receiver who catches five of ten passes can call that a great game or a terrible one. The stats don't decide which story gets told - he does.

Keep telling yourself you're the guy who loses, and you'll keep proving yourself right.

What story have you been telling yourself about your own setbacks?

#kevintrudeau #mindset #success #mentaltoughness #poolchampion #comeback

clips.caption:
Charlie Keating died with a smile on his face.

It wasn't the $400,000 death benefit his wife would collect. It had nothing to do with money at all.

He smiled because he'd given his life to something he actually believed in.

Most people never get that. They spend decades dying slowly, one quiet day at a time, for something they would never have actually given their life for if you asked them straight out.

Are you building toward something you'd die for, or just drifting through it?
